executiveSummary: GM0579 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its CBS/PDOK 2025 identity, 26,058-person municipality control, 15 neighbourhoods in five districts, one BAG place, one BRT settlement, 43 scheduled-transit stop areas, zero conventional rail stations and five NWB logical links are coherent; rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 26,055, only three below the separately published control (-0.012%). Release is nevertheless correction-required. Oegstgeest is a dense municipality divided by the Rijnland-boezem Oegstgeesterkanaal, with official regional-defence flood footprints, neighbourhood-specific pluvial, groundwater and heat vulnerabilities, the A44 and Rijnzichtweg/N206 access system, a developing Leiden Bio Science Park area west of the A44 and LUMC Curium clinical youth-psychiatry occupancy. The model instead reports a generic coastal legacy inundation amplitude of 2.028226 from T+6 through T+24, 12,818 affected resident-equivalents and 302,136.577 deprived person-hours at T+24 without a selected North Sea boundary, primary defence, regional defence, Rijnland path, connected footprint, arrival or recession. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset likewise fixes 0.559232 from T+12 through T+72 without a selected major-river connection. Pluvial reports 0.571319 at T+12/T+24 without event-valid rainfall, terrain, sewer, groundwater, pump or boezem state. Eight unrelated active presets reuse effectively the same resident-led neighbourhood order, contradicting the municipality's published maps: regional-defence flooding highlights west Voscuyl, Haaswijk-Oost, De Morsebel and Poelgeest, while pluvial risk highlights Oranje Nassau, Voscuyl and Bloemenbuurt. Public context identifies eight water assets, about 50 km of drainage with unverified technical condition, Dunea's river-to-Berkheide supply dependency, one electricity-planning sample, 36 antennas, 17 education uses and no acute-care point inside the boundary; these do not establish live topology, capacity, backup or restoration. Coastal, major-river, regional-water, pluvial, groundwater and sewer mechanisms must remain separate, and Unknown, NoData, catalogue no-match and static register status must never become zero, safe, open or operational.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0579 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region data
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0579 as Oegstgeest in Zuid-Holland and Hollands-Midden and report 26,058 residents, density 3,573/km², 21.6% aged 65 or older and 3,862 one-person households; the generated centre [4.475263383795309,52.185732331041145] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Fifteen neighbourhood rows in five districts sum to 26,055 residents, three below the separately rounded municipality control (-0.012%); households sum to 11,250 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 5,625. Model allocation reconciles to the control without rewriting observations.
BAG and BRT each supply one named Oegstgeest place/woonkern. Oranje Nassau has 4,440 residents, Nieuw-Rhijngeest 3,585, Haaswijk-Oost 2,800, Poelgeest 2,615 and Bloemenbuurt 2,580.

CBS regional statistics expose 36 fields. District heating and public charging are null in all 15 rows and cars per household is null in one; CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0. Null and suppression remain NoData rather than numeric zero.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Oegstgeest municipal risk profile
evidenceSources.edition: Current public municipal profile inspected 3 September 2026; underlying context has mixed source dates
supports: VRHM describes Oegstgeest as a densely built village near Leiden and The Hague and identifies the A44 through the municipality. This is static risk context, not a live accessibility state.

The profile identifies establishments with hazardous substances in or near Oegstgeest, including Leiden Bio Science Park and AkzoNobel, and lists flooding, extreme weather, wildfire/smoke and interruptions to electricity, gas, drinking water, wastewater, telecom and food among regional risk classes.

Risk-profile inclusion establishes scenario eligibility only. It does not identify a current release, target, plume, flood footprint, outage, casualty, route closure, evacuation order or first-72-hour resource state.
The site is publicly viewable but no standard redistribution licence, stable machine API or guaranteed update cadence was identified during this audit.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Klimaatadaptatiestrategie Oegstgeest 2023–2028
evidenceSources.edition: Dossier W0218 dated 10 January 2023; municipal publication linked 1 February 2024
supports: The Oegstgeesterkanaal is part of Rijnland's boezem, receives polder water and ultimately drains through the Koning Willem-Alexandergemaal at Katwijk. The canal separates Haaswijk and is a materially different mechanism from open-coast or Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation.

The selected regional-defence failure study maps partial vulnerability in four areas: west Voscuyl, including sports fields up to 2.5 m and much of west Voscuyl around 0.5 m; Haaswijk-Oost and De Morsebel up to 1 m; and Poelgeest around 1.5–2.5 m. Areas outside that selected study footprint cannot be generalized as flood-safe.

For pluvial flooding, the strategy identifies Oranje Nassau, Voscuyl and Bloemenbuurt as highest risk and Haaswijk-West/East as lower because nearby surface water receives drainage. It reports 20–50 cm facade contact in Oranje Nassau, Voscuyl, Bloemenbuurt and Poelgeest, and difficult access on Rijnzichtweg on both sides of the A44 and in De Kempenaerstraat. It also cautions that Oranje Nassau was recently redesigned, so mapped analysis may already overstate current susceptibility.

Naturally high or variable groundwater, pre-1970 timber-pile foundations in Oranje Nassau/Voscuyl, and drought-sensitive Park Rhijngeest/Oud-Poelgeest are distinct pathways. Published heat hotspots include Bloemenbuurt/Lange Voort/Ommevoort, Oranjepark, the area west of the A44 and artificial-turf areas; these are scenario/planning maps rather than observations or forecasts.

The strategy aims to keep main and emergency routes usable and to protect care facilities, monuments and vital infrastructure, but provides no incident-authorised action feed, real-time resources or guaranteed outcome. The PDF expressly restricts reproduction/use without client permission, so licence must be resolved before machine redistribution.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Oegstgeest / Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Integral Water Chain Programme 2024–2028 and public water-asset context
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive measure module dated 26 September 2023; HWH deployment snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: The programme states that groundwater is naturally high in parts of Oegstgeest and records about 50 km of drainage, largely connected to storm-sewer manholes and watercourses. Twenty-one groundwater points are read four times yearly; this is sparse monitoring, not a continuous municipal field.

It explicitly states there is no insight into the technical condition of drainage facilities and no complete overview of complaints/reports. Oudenhof measures include sewer separation and retention, and sewer-replacement pressure peaks from 2030 to 2050. Unknown condition cannot become available capacity or an all-clear.

Full-boundary assignment in the HWH deployment snapshot finds eight points: one Oegstgeest wastewater pump and seven surface-water pumps. Registered capacities include 1,180 register units for the wastewater point and 2.33–15 for six surface-water pumps, while one is null; units, topology and operational comparability are unverified.

HWH IMWA/DAMO is contributor-dependent/partial and CC BY-SA 4.0, with weekly refresh where contributors supply data. Status 'gerealiseerd' is registered existence, not live operation, power/backup, telemetry, overflow, water quality, catchment control or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — LUMC Curium Oegstgeest and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Current LUMC service page inspected 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: LUMC Curium at Endegeesterstraatweg 27 in Oegstgeest provides day-clinical and clinical child and adolescent psychiatry. In clinical care, patients can stay during evenings and nights; the site includes High & Intensive Care and an acute-psychiatry route.

This official site presence means overnight and assisted populations cannot be inferred from registered residents alone. The page does not disclose incident occupancy, mobility needs, staff, medicines, generator endurance, water stock, evacuation capability or current acceptance.

RIVM acute-care v1.1, a CC0 static survey dataset, assigns no emergency department inside GM0579. LUMC Leiden is the nearest listed acute-care location at 2.18 km straight-line and reports a 24/7 emergency department; distance and reported service are not event-valid travel time, route access, occupancy or guaranteed acceptance.

Local Curium continuity and external LUMC access are separate dependencies. Neither an empty local acute-care match nor a nearby external point proves service absence, route availability or sufficient capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — A44/N206/N444, rail and scheduled-transit access context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; RWS article published 19 May 2026; GTFS version 9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB graph has five logical boundary links but only three physical identities: A44 toward Leiden and Teylingen, N206 toward Leiden and Katwijk, and N444 toward Teylingen. Paired A44 and N206 records are consecutive series edges and their nominal 260/150 scenario units are non-additive, not measured emergency capacity.

Rijkswaterstaat's 2026 A44 closure notice identifies Oegstgeest exit 8 and rerouting through A4, N443 and N206. A historic works notice proves corridor identity and possible alternatives only, not current closure, capacity, travel time or hazard passability.

No conventional ProRail station lies inside GM0579. GTFS version 9543 assigns 43 stop areas, including Bio Science Park-West, CORPUS, Curium and Endegeest; schedule/geometry does not establish vehicles, passengers, accessibility, evacuation role or current operation.

The municipal climate strategy separately identifies extreme-rain difficulty on Rijnzichtweg on both sides of A44. NWB municipal-node links do not represent this internal choke point, local care access, direction, bridges/tunnels, closure, destination or onward LUMC reachability.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Oegstgeest drinking-water service area and river–dune supply dependency
evidenceSources.edition: Drinkwatervoorziening van de toekomst 2030–2040 planning document; current service-area terms published for 2026
supports: Dunea identifies Oegstgeest within its northern supply area, primarily served through the Berkheide dune production area near Katwijk.

The public system description says dune freshwater is insufficient alone and is supplemented with pretreated river water from the Afgedamde Maas and Lek; the approximate 10/90 precipitation-to-river-water ratio is a planning/system description, not incident flow or reserve.

This dependency can support a safe aggregate service-area relationship, but does not establish sensitive distribution topology, current source quality, storage, pressure, failure, isolation, backup endurance or restoration.
The PDF is public planning evidence without a machine incident feed or a standard reuse licence identified during this audit. It must not directly drive exact first-72-hour Water availability.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM / KNMI / Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Electricity planning, communications, education, air-quality, weather and water-observation context
supports: One postcode sample at 2343SR maps to Liander OS RIJNSBURG 10-1i and reports planning withdrawal of 44/34 MW existing/required, a 5.7 MW queue and ten requests; injection is 55/13 MW with a 10 MW queue and null request count. Eleven projects include dates from 2026. One sample is not complete coverage, live load, reserve, switching, outage or restoration, and an exact licence identifier was not found.

RDI assigns 36 antenna installations: 15 mobile, seven fixed-link, nine amateur and five broadcast. DUO assigns 17 education uses: nine primary, three secondary, three special and two other. RDI states no standard licence/cadence; DUO RIO is daily attribution-licensed register data. Points do not establish coverage, occupancy, support-site role, backup or operation.

No Luchtmeetnet station lies in GM0579; De Zilk is nearest at 12.56 km. No KNMI observation station lies inside; Voorschoten is nearest at 5.76 km and its cached 2 September 2026 23:30Z record reports 18.4°C, 7.81 m/s gust and zero hourly rain. External point observations are not municipal hazard surfaces or canonical T+0.

No Waterinfo observation/forecast point is assigned inside GM0579; Scheveningen is nearest at 17.37 km. No local match is scoped NoData, not zero water or safe state. KNMI observations are ten-minute CC BY 4.0; Waterinfo is CC0 public/non-mission-critical context whose issue, validity and horizon must travel with each value.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Safety magazine and 72-hour household preparedness guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal safety-magazine page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Municipal guidance tells residents to prepare an emergency kit for the first 72 hours. Advice is a preparedness objective, not evidence that a household has water, food, medicines, radio, power or a support network.

The magazine warns that extreme rainfall can also flood emergency-service buildings and delay assistance. This is qualitative preparedness context, not a facility-specific depth, outage or response time.

The public page does not expose exercised local support points, shelter/evacuation zones, care transport, dewatering resources, route-clearance teams, stocks, staff, restoration milestones or verified re-entry criteria.
No standard machine API, reuse licence, incident validity window or update service was identified; public guidance must remain separate from authorised actions and verified execution.

residualLimitations: This is an audit of a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a KNMI/WMCN/VRHM warning, hydraulic forecast, evacuation order, hazardous-material alert, outage statement, route guarantee, casualty estimate or operator restoration commitment.
CBS 2025 neighbourhood figures are rounded/suppressed and need not sum exactly to the municipality control; allocation reconciliation does not rewrite the published three-person difference.

The generalized administrative boundary cannot represent the Oegstgeesterkanaal, polders, primary/regional defences, sewer/drainage catchments, groundwater, buildings, roads or exact hazard intersections.

The 2023 climate strategy is official planning/scenario evidence, not a live forecast; it notes that Oranje Nassau redesign may have changed the underlying pluvial result, and its PDF does not grant standard reuse.
A bounded LIWO candidate-point no-match does not establish absence of a connected primary/regional-defence footprint, and an unselected scenario is Unknown rather than safe.

The eight HWH points have contributor-dependent completeness and do not establish connected topology, compatible capacity units, telemetry, power/backup, live state, overflow, water quality or restoration.

The water-chain programme explicitly lacks technical-condition insight and complete complaint records; 21 points read four times yearly cannot become continuous groundwater or drainage-state coverage.

Dunea public planning documents identify service-area and source/transport/dune dependencies but not sensitive topology, current storage/quality/flow, outage, redundancy, backup endurance or restoration.
NWB, RWS notices, GTFS, RIVM, NBNL, RDI and DUO data do not establish live passability, passengers, occupancy, acceptance, physical utility topology, coverage, capacity, backup or repair.

Curium clinical presence and Bio Science Park/hazardous-material context do not disclose incident occupancy, patient mobility, staff, inventory, release, plume, generator, medicine, water or evacuation state.
No local Waterinfo, KNMI or Luchtmeetnet point means scoped NoData. External station values cannot establish Oegstgeest rainfall, boezem level, air quality, flood depth or canonical T+0.

The canonical wildfire's zero direct flame is a narrow model statement, not proof of zero vegetation/fire risk; no authorised local ignition, fuel/moisture, perimeter, smoke plume, access or suppression state is selected.
The tiny cached seismic catalogue and zero post-T+6 modeled motion do not prove no induced or tectonic risk; no event-specific KNMI shakemap or vulnerability inventory is ingested.
A generic cyber preset has no named target, incident report, affected systems, clock, scope or recovery evidence and must not reveal or invent sensitive topology.

Household 72-hour guidance is not evidence of actual supplies. Support points, shelters, mutual aid, care acceptance, staffing, crews, fuel, stocks, dewatering, inspection, re-entry and recovery beyond T+72 remain unverified.
